answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a river tag. The dawn cap is policed at intake and ocean shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, as each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 16 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
